findings.reason: the section should keep the reader in `_backends.py` (adding its string-refusal there, where a bare string is currently dropped silently) and add only the `_schema_view` pop in flight.py, rather than declare a parallel reader that can drift from the one §7 already seeds from.
findings.text: §11 proposes adding "a reader in `reckon/flight.py`" that "accepts [worker_mcp_servers] only as a list of server names", but `_declared_worker_mcp_servers` at `reckon/_backends.py:2233` already reads the same key from the resolved flight config and normalises it to a server-name list (it is the function `_seed_worker_mcp_settings` is seeded from at `reckon/_backends.py:3318`), so the plan forks a second reader of one key and normalises it twice; the owner to extend is `_declared_worker_mcp_servers`, and the only genuinely new work §11 needs is the `_schema_view` admission

findings.reason: §2 should either add `reckon/velocity.py` to its write paths and extract the walk into a shared helper the promotion-receipt reader and the census both call, or drop the reuse claim and name the duplication it accepts.
findings.text: §2 states its transcript count "walks their tool-result blocks with the content-block walk the promotion-receipt reader in `reckon/velocity.py` already uses" while also stating "the transcript count calls `reckon/velocity.py` and changes nothing in it", but that walk is not a reusable function — it is inline in `promotion_receipts` at `reckon/velocity.py:1576-1594` (the tool_use/tool_result loop over `record["message"]["content"]`), so a census that changes nothing in velocity.py must copy the loop into `reckon/mcp_census.py`, giving two implementations of the transcript content-block walk that drift as the transcript schema is touched

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §2's `reckon/mcp_census.py` hides the window, the pattern table, the cause classification and the transcript count behind a single census function the doctor block calls; §5 and §11 add no module.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §11 declares "a reader in `reckon/flight.py`" for `worker_mcp_servers`, but `_declared_worker_mcp_servers` at `reckon/_backends.py:2233` already reads and validates that exact key from the resolved flight config (called at `reckon/_backends.py:3318`); and §2 claims to reuse velocity's content-block walk while changing nothing in `reckon/velocity.py`, but that walk is inline in `promotion_receipts` (`reckon/velocity.py:1576-1594`), so reuse requires either editing velocity.py or duplicating the walk.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — §2 states in its own text that the check "adds no command and no option", §5 adds a block to the existing `reckon doctor` report and names no option, and §11 admits an existing key already read by `_declared_worker_mcp_servers` rather than adding a new family; none of §2, §5, §11 extends cli_options (336), mcp_views (33) or refusal_families (23).
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §2 now cites `transcript_index` (`reckon/velocity.py:1363`) as the owner of locating Claude Code transcripts rather than walking `~/.claude/projects` itself, and cites the content-block walk the promotion-receipt reader uses; §5 extends doctor's existing MCP-config reader (`reckon/project_maintenance_commands.py:896-935`); §11 cites the `SPRINT_RECENT_DAYS_KEY`/`HARNESS_HOME_FILES` reckon-owned-key pattern in `reckon/flight.py`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §2's census adds log parsing and a pattern table no existing reader has, and §5's launch check adds path/directory validation, rather than forwarding to an existing reader.
